nodes.title: SG-2 Implement game runtime and The Boy's Room content
nodes.body:
Context: the repo currently holds only the Go backend (backend/) and context.md; there is no game module yet, so the TypeScript game package is created in the new folder backend/game/ (the only existing top-level folder is backend/). Desired behavior: backend/game/src/engine, backend/game/src/state and backend/game/src/systems hold pure functions over a serializable GameState covering scenes, clickable objects with actions (inspect, push, search, leave), dialogue, choices, events, inventory, conditions, world flags and scene transitions. A YAML loader plus validator reads backend/game/content/worlds/the-boys-room/world.yaml and scenes/bedroom.yaml and reports unknown scene/object/character/flag references. Expected result: bedroom content with the opening question, bed, bookshelf with a persistent hidden door, desk, old computer, window and door, all covered by Vitest. Why: players must be able to play and the community must be able to extend content without rewriting the engine.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a GameState, when any runtime function is called, then it returns a new state object and never mutates its input, and the state survives JSON.stringify/JSON.parse unchanged.
- Given the content files, when the loader runs, then it returns a typed world, and unknown scene, object, character or flag references yield error strings naming the reference.
- Given the bedroom scene, when it is loaded, then it contains the opening dialogue 'I don't know what to do next. What should we do?', bed, bookshelf, desk, old computer, window and door.
- Given the bookshelf search action was performed, when state is serialized, restored and the scene viewed again, then the secret door is still open.
- Given Vitest unit tests, when they run, then each system, the reference validator with invalid fixtures and persistence are covered and pass.


## Scope
- In scope: backend/game/ TypeScript runtime modules
- In scope: YAML loader and validator
- In scope: the-boys-room world and bedroom YAML
- In scope: Vitest unit tests
- Out of scope: React rendering
- Out of scope: backend API changes
- Out of scope: worker and round lifecycle
- Out of scope: pixel art assets
- Preserve: Existing Go code in backend/ (go.mod, cmd, internal) unchanged


## Technical constraints
- TypeScript with Vitest
- Content is declarative YAML parsed with the yaml npm package
- All runtime functions are pure over serializable state
- No database


## Definition of done
- All four requirements have Act and Verify units completed
- Vitest suite passes


## Non-functional requirements
- Strict TypeScript typing


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Pure runtime systems over serializable game state
nodes.body:
Context: no game runtime exists. Desired behavior: a GameState (currentScene, inventory, discoveredObjects, completedQuests, relationships, flags, history, activeDialogue) and pure systems that evaluate conditions, apply events, run object actions, advance dialogue and switch scenes. Expected result: every function takes state and returns a new state. Why: deterministic, testable, persistable gameplay.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a state and an action with events set_flag, add_item, goto_scene, when performAction runs, then the returned state has the flag, item and new currentScene and the original state is unchanged.
- Given a condition {flag,equals} or {has_item}, when evaluated, then it returns true or false matching the state.
- Given a dialogue node with choices, when a choice is selected, then its events are applied, history records it and the next node becomes active.
- Given an action whose conditions fail, when performed, then the state is returned unchanged.


## Scope
- In scope: backend/game/src/state
- In scope: backend/game/src/systems
- In scope: backend/game/src/engine scene logic
- Out of scope: YAML parsing
- Out of scope: UI


## Technical constraints
- Pure functions, no I/O
- Action ids limited to inspect, push, search, leave


## Definition of done
- Modules compile under tsc strict


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · YAML content loader and reference validator
nodes.body:
Context: content is declarative YAML. Desired behavior: loadWorld(dir) reads world.yaml and each listed scene file and returns {world,scenes}; validateWorld returns error strings for unknown scene, object, character and flag references. Expected result: content authors get precise errors. Why: coding agents add content safely.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a valid content directory, when loadWorld runs, then it returns the world and every scene listed in world.yaml.
- Given a goto_scene event to an unknown scene, when validated, then an error names the scene.

- Given a missing scene file or malformed YAML, when loaded, then loadWorld throws an error naming the file.

nodes.title: REQ · Persistent world state serialization
nodes.body:
Context: state is plain data. Desired behavior: serializeState/deserializeState convert GameState to and from JSON with validation, and the scene view reflects restored flags. Expected result: opening the secret door, saving, restoring and returning to the room shows it still open. Why: the world must remember meaningful actions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given malformed JSON or missing fields, when deserialized, then an error is thrown.
- Given the bookshelf searched, when state is round-tripped and getSceneView is called, then bookshelf open is true.

- In scope: backend/game/src/state/persistence.ts
- Out of scope: browser storage, backend save API


## Technical constraints
- Pure JSON string conversion, no storage access

nodes.summary: Create game package config, types, state, conditions, inventory, events, dialogue and scene engine
nodes.description: Create the game TypeScript package under backend/game and the pure runtime modules. Context: backend/game does not exist. Desired behavior: types define content and state shapes; systems operate immutably. Expected result: modules importable by loader and tests.
acceptance_criteria: Given the package, when tsc --noEmit runs, then it compiles with strict mode.
Given any system function, when called, then the input state is not mutated.
technical_constraints: package.json scripts: test = vitest run, typecheck = tsc --noEmit

steps.action: Create package.json with type module, scripts test='vitest run' and typecheck='tsc --noEmit', dependency yaml, devDependencies typescript and vitest; also create tsconfig.json (strict true, module ESNext, moduleResolution Bundler, target ES2022, include src and tests) and vitest.config.ts using defineConfig with test.include ['tests/**/*.test.ts'].
steps.expected: npm install in backend/game succeeds and vitest/tsc binaries exist.

steps.action: Create tsconfig.json with compilerOptions strict true, module ESNext, moduleResolution Bundler, target ES2022, noEmit true, types [] and include ['src','tests'].
Create vitest.config.ts exporting default defineConfig({test:{include:['tests/**/*.test.ts']}}) imported from 'vitest/config'.
steps.code:
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
export default defineConfig({ test: { include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts'] } });
steps.expected: vitest discovers only files under tests/.

steps.symbol: new: Condition, GameEvent, ActionDef, ObjectDef, DialogueNode, SceneDef, WorldDef, GameState
steps.action: Export types: Condition = {flag:string;equals?:boolean}|{hasItem:string}; GameEvent = set_flag{flag,value}|add_item{item}|remove_item{item}|goto_scene{scene}|say{character,text}|show_text{text}|discover{object}; ActionDef{id:'inspect'|'push'|'search'|'leave';label;conditions?:Condition[];events:GameEvent[]}; ObjectDef{id,name,description,actions,openWhenFlag?}; DialogueNode{id,speaker,text,choices:{text;next?;events?}[]}; SceneDef{id,title,objects,openingDialogue?:string(node id),dialogue:DialogueNode[]}; WorldDef{id,title,startScene,scenes:string[],characters:{id,name}[],flags:string[]}; GameState{currentScene,inventory:string[],discoveredObjects:string[],completedQuests:string[],relationships:Record<string,number>,flags:Record<string,boolean>,history:string[],activeDialogue:string|null}.

Implement createInitialState(world:WorldDef,scene:SceneDef):GameState with currentScene=world.startScene, empty collections, activeDialogue=scene.openingDialogue??null; setFlag(state,flag,value) returning {...state,flags:{...state.flags,[flag]:value}}; addHistory(state,line) returning a new state with line appended.
steps.expected: Functions return new objects; inputs unchanged.

steps.action: evaluateCondition(state,c) returns state.flags[c.flag]===(c.equals??true) for flag conditions and state.inventory.includes(c.hasItem) for hasItem conditions; evaluateAll(state,conds?) returns true when conds is undefined/empty or every condition passes.
addItem returns state with item appended only if absent; removeItem returns state with item filtered out; hasItem returns state.inventory.includes(item).

applyEvent switches on event.type: set_flag->setFlag, add_item->addItem, remove_item->removeItem, goto_scene->{...state,currentScene:event.scene,activeDialogue:null} with history 'Went to <scene>', say->addHistory '<character>: <text>', show_text->addHistory text, discover->add object id to discoveredObjects once; applyEvents reduces a list in order.

getActiveNode(state,scene) returns the DialogueNode matching state.activeDialogue or undefined; chooseOption(state,scene,index) applies the choice's events via applyEvents, appends history of the choice text, and sets activeDialogue to choice.next??null; returns state unchanged when node or index is invalid.
steps.expected: Choice advances dialogue and records history.

steps.action: getSceneView(state,scene) returns objects each with only the actions whose conditions pass, plus an open:boolean computed from openWhenFlag in state.flags; performAction(state,scene,objectId,actionId) finds the action, returns state unchanged if object/action missing or evaluateAll fails, otherwise returns applyEvents(state,action.events).
